items.title: When Transparency Changes the System
items.topic: how publishing performance data can improve accountability while also changing the behavior that the data were meant to measure
items.benefit: public information can help citizens compare institutions, identify problems, and pressure organizations to improve weak performance
items.challenge: once a measure becomes highly visible, institutions may redirect effort toward the published indicator, alter reporting practices, or avoid difficult cases
items.lesson: transparency is most informative when designers anticipate behavioral responses and combine published metrics with independent checks and broader evidence
items.topicJa: 成果データの公開が説明責任を高める一方で測定対象の行動自体を変える問題
items.benefitJa: 公開情報によって市民が組織を比較し問題を見つけ改善を促せること
items.challengeJa: 指標が注目されると組織が公開値だけに努力を集中したり報告方法や対象選択を変えたりする可能性があること
items.lessonJa: 透明性を有効にするには行動変化を予想し独立確認や幅広い証拠と組み合わせる必要がある

items.title: The Value of Reversible Decisions
items.topic: why uncertainty can make a flexible and reversible policy more valuable than a seemingly optimal but difficult-to-change commitment
items.benefit: a strong long-term commitment can provide certainty, reduce repeated decision costs, and support investments that require stable expectations
items.challenge: when evidence is incomplete or conditions change quickly, an irreversible choice can lock institutions into costs that were not visible at the start
items.lesson: decision quality depends not only on expected benefits today but also on the option value of learning and adapting tomorrow
items.topicJa: 不確実な状況では最適に見える固定的決定より変更可能な政策に価値がある理由
items.benefitJa: 長期的な確約は予測可能性を高め繰り返しの判断コストを減らし安定を必要とする投資を支えられること
items.challengeJa: 証拠が不十分で状況変化が速いと取り消しにくい選択が当初見えなかった費用を固定する可能性があること
items.lessonJa: 判断の質は現在の期待利益だけでなく将来学び修正できる選択肢の価値にも左右される

items.title: Evidence From Those Who Remain
items.topic: how conclusions about a program can become biased when the people who leave differ systematically from those who stay
items.benefit: following participants over time can reveal whether an intervention produces durable changes rather than short-lived effects
items.challenge: if dissatisfied, mobile, or highly burdened participants are more likely to disappear from follow-up, the remaining sample may look more successful than the original group
items.lesson: longitudinal evidence should report attrition, investigate who is missing, and test how plausible missing outcomes would change the conclusion
items.topicJa: 継続参加者だけのデータで事業効果を判断すると偏りが生じる問題
items.benefitJa: 参加者を長期追跡すると一時的でなく持続的な変化か確認できること
items.challengeJa: 不満がある人や移動する人や負担の大きい人ほど追跡から消えると残った集団が実際より成功して見えること
items.lessonJa: 長期データでは脱落率と欠測者の特徴を示し欠けた結果が結論をどう変えるか検討する必要がある

items.title: Fairness Across Time
items.topic: the conflict between policies that maximize immediate benefits and investments whose costs are paid now while benefits arrive for future generations
items.benefit: prioritizing current needs can relieve urgent hardship and direct limited resources toward people whose problems are already visible
items.challenge: delaying maintenance, environmental protection, or preventive investment may transfer larger risks and costs to people who had no voice in the original decision
items.lesson: fair policy analysis should make intergenerational tradeoffs explicit and examine who receives benefits, who bears costs, and when each occurs
items.topicJa: 現在の利益を最大化する政策と将来世代のための投資が衝突する問題
items.benefitJa: 現在の必要を優先すると差し迫った困難を軽減し限られた資源を目に見える問題へ向けられること
items.challengeJa: 保守や環境保護や予防投資を遅らせると決定に参加できない将来の人々へより大きなリスクと費用を移す可能性があること
items.lessonJa: 公平な政策分析では世代間のトレードオフを明示し誰がいつ利益と費用を負うか検討する必要がある
